title: Extension by zero under a proper modification
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $\pi:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $U'=Y\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], let $j':U'\hookrightarrow Y$ be its open immersion and $h:U'\to U$ its projection, and assume $h$ is an isomorphism. For any sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], put $G'=h^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. With extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the canonical adjunction map is an isomorphism and the positive higher direct images vanish:
$$
 j_!G\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*j'_!G',\qquad R^q\pi_*j'_!G'=0\quad(q>0).
$$
Here the canonical map is adjoint under $\pi^{-1}\dashv\pi_*$ to the inverse of the extension-by-zero base-change map $j'_!h^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^{-1}j_!G$. No finiteness or constructibility of $G$ and no invertibility assumption on $\#\Lambda$ is required.

proof.text: Write $F=j'_!G'$ and $E=j_!G$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] to the cartesian square $(j',h,\pi,j)$: an open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and the general etale extension construction is exactly the open extension by zero: by [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], the indexing set $\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$ has at most one member, giving the same presheaf before sheafification. This gives $b:F\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^{-1}E$. The adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives the $\Lambda$-linear map $a=\pi_*(b^{-1})\circ\eta_{\pi,E}:E\to\pi_*F$. This fixes the map whose stalks will be tested.

proof.text: Fix any geometric point $\bar x:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, put $Y_{\bar x}=Y\times_XP$, and denote its projections by $i:Y_{\bar x}\to Y$ and $r:Y_{\bar x}\to P$. Apply the derived formula of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] to $\pi$ and $K=F[0]$. It gives the canonical exchange isomorphism $\bar x^{-1}R\pi_*F\simeq Rr_*i^{-1}F$. This formula requires only a finite ring and a bounded-below complex, not finite stalks of $F$. Properness is exactly the hypothesis on $\pi$, and $F[0]$ is bounded below.

Suppose $\bar x$ lies outside $U$. Every geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y_{\bar x}$ maps outside $U'$: a point in $U'$ would have image in $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], $F_{i\bar y}=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], $(i^{-1}F)_{\bar y}=F_{i\bar y}=0$ on underlying abelian sheaves. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to i^{-1}F$ to get $i^{-1}F=0$; a module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero. Consequently step 2 gives $\bar x^{-1}R\pi_*F=0$ (the zero complex is an injective resolution of zero). Also $E_{\bar x}=0$ by the same extension-by-zero stalk lemma.

Suppose instead $\bar x=j\bar u$ lies in $U$. The universal property of the fibre product gives $Y\times_XP=(Y\times_XU)\times_UP=U'\times_UP$. Base-changing the inverse of $h$ supplies an inverse to $r:Y_{\bar x}\to P$; hence the fibre is $P$ as a scheme, not only a singleton of points. Let $\bar y:P\to Y$ be the resulting lift of $\bar x$, and $\bar u':P\to U'$ its factorization, so $h\bar u'=\bar u$. The stalk formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied also to $h$, give $F_{\bar y}=(G')_{\bar u'}=(h^{-1}G)_{\bar u'}\cong G_{\bar u}$ and $E_{\bar x}\cong G_{\bar u}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], $\Gamma(P,i^{-1}F)\cong F_{\bar y}$ and sections on $P_{\Et}$ are exact. Under the scheme isomorphism $r$, direct image is identity (on an etale object its defining fibre product is that object), so applying it to an injective resolution leaves that resolution unchanged; thus $Rr_*i^{-1}F$ has degree-zero cohomology $i^{-1}F$ and zero positive cohomology.
In degree zero the canonical exchange in step 2 is the underived exchange: [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] (3) identifies its underlying abelian morphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] computes that morphism using underived exchange on an injective resolution. Naturality of underived exchange with the augmentation $F[0]\to I$ identifies the degree-zero map with $\operatorname{Ex}^0_F$ (exact inverse image preserves the degree-zero kernel, and left exact direct image identifies it with the direct image of $F$). The representative-section formula of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], together with [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], sends a section over $V\times_XY$ to its pullback on $(V\times_XY)\times_YP$, followed by evaluation at the point above $\bar v$. Write $t:(\pi_*F)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(P,i^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar y}$ for this degree-zero isomorphism. For a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar x$ and $s\in E(V)$, $a$ sends $s$ to $b^{-1}(\eta_{\pi,E}(V)s)$ on $V\times_XY$. Therefore $b_{\bar y}t a_{\bar x}$ sends the germ of $s$ to the germ of $\eta_{\pi,E}(V)s$. The compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] gives $c_{\pi,\bar y,E}\,b_{\bar y}\,t\,a_{\bar x}=\mathrm{id}_{E_{\bar x}}$. Every stalk element has such a representative, and $c_{\pi,\bar y,E}$, $b_{\bar y}$ and $t$ are isomorphisms; hence $a_{\bar x}=(c_{\pi,\bar y,E}b_{\bar y}t)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Naturality with respect to scalar endomorphisms makes all these identifications $\Lambda$-linear.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], $\Gamma(P,\bar x^{-1}M)=M_{\bar x}$ and $\Gamma(P,-)$ is exact. Inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so taking degree $q$ cohomology of step 2 and then sections computes $(R^q\pi_*F)_{\bar x}$. Steps 3 and 4 show it is zero for every $q>0$ at every geometric point, and show $a$ is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk in degree zero. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to R^q\pi_*F$ and to $a$ on underlying abelian sheaves. A bijective linear sheaf map has a linear inverse, and zero underlying abelian sheaf means zero module sheaf. Therefore $a$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-module sheaves and all $R^q\pi_*F$, $q>0$, vanish.
